newsitem.title: USA: Copley to evaluate possible alliances.
newsitem.headline: Copley to evaluate possible alliances.

text.p: Copley Pharmaceutical Inc said on Thursday it had received inquiries about "possible business alliances."
The generic drug company said it had hired Oppenheimer & Co Inc to evaluate strategic alternatives for the company, including the possible alliances.
It gave no further details and spokesmen were not immediately available.
The statement came with the company's third quarter report of net income of $614,000 or $0.03 per share compared to a net loss of $5.2 million or $0.28 per share for the third quarter of 1995.
Copley President Kenneth Larsen said that although the company has posted profits for two consecutive quarters, it still faced challenges.
"It is widely acknowledged that these are highly competitive and challenging times for the entire generic industry," Larsen said in the company statement.
"Certainly we are not alone as we strive to increase profitability despite eroding prices and narrowing margins," he added.
Copley's third quarter net sales were $32.6 million, compared to $39.2 million for the third quarter of 1995.

It said its "sales and overall profitability continue to be adversely affected by the significant price decrease on glyburide," its major distributed product. It also cited continued price erosion across the company's product line.

Other factors affecting the quarterly results included the negative impact of the filing for bankruptcy protection by a major customer, which was offset by the settlement of an insurance claim, Copley said.
